title: A representable category fibred in groupoids over a stack is a stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes, and let $q:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism over $S$-schemes. Categories fibred in groupoids, their morphisms, 2-fibre products and the discrete fibred groupoid $h_P$ of a scheme use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose $\mathcal G$ is a stack for etale coverings: isomorphisms form sheaves and descent data for objects are effective. Suppose that for every scheme $T\to\mathcal G$, the fibred groupoid $T\times_{\mathcal G}\mathcal F$ is equivalent over $T$-schemes to $h_{P_T}$ for some $T$-scheme $P_T$. Then $\mathcal F$ is a stack for etale coverings. No finiteness, smoothness, surjectivity, or stack hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic), stack assertion, scheme-representable specialization. Its proof uses only the sheaf property of the represented relative fibres, so applies verbatim to etale coverings and the etale-stack convention here.

proof.text: For an $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal G(T)$, write $K_y(V)$ for the groupoid of pairs $(x,\theta:q(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y|_V)$ over $V\to T$. Its arrows $a:(x,\theta)\to(x',\theta')$ satisfy $\theta' q(a)=\theta$. This is the 2-fibre product in the hypothesis using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: its comparison is $\theta^{-1}:y|_V\to q(x)$, so its arrow equation is $q(a)\theta^{-1}=(\theta')^{-1}$, equivalently $\theta' q(a)=\theta$. Choose its assumed equivalence with $h_{P_T}$. Thus its isomorphism classes identify with $\operatorname{Mor}_T(V,P_T)$. These bijections commute with restriction: an equivalence over $T$-schemes preserves cartesian pullbacks, and the resulting comparison isomorphisms become equalities after passing to isomorphism classes. Between any two fixed objects of $K_y(V)$ there is at most one arrow, since full faithfulness identifies that set with a hom-set of a discrete groupoid. In particular $q:\mathcal F(T)\to\mathcal G(T)$ is faithful. Indeed, if $q(a)=q(b)$ for $a,b:x\to x'$, both $a$ and $b$ are arrows from $(x,q(a))$ to $(x',\mathrm{id})$ in $K_{q(x')}(T)$, so $a=b$.

source.place: Tag 0CKJ (lemma-relative-sheaf-over-stack-is-stack), hypothesis (2), verified directly from the represented relative groupoid; scheme-representable input from algebraic.tex, Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic)

proof.text: Fix $T,y$ as in step 1 and restrict $K_y$ to the small etale site of $T$. The scheme $P_T$ need not be etale, finite, or separated over $T$. Nevertheless [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] applies to this arbitrary $T$-scheme: for each object $U\to T$ of this small site and each etale cover $(U_i\to U)$, compatible $T$-morphisms $U_i\to P_T$ glue uniquely to a $T$-morphism $U\to P_T$. Compatibility here is equality after restriction to the exact overlaps $U_i\times_U U_j$ appearing in the cited sheaf statement. Through the restriction-compatible bijections of step 1, the presheaf of isomorphism classes of pairs $(x,\theta)$ therefore has the same existence and uniqueness of gluing on this site. We use this only for covers of $T$ and their overlaps; since $T$ is arbitrary, no assertion about all objects of a big site is needed.

source.place: Tag 0CKJ (lemma-relative-sheaf-over-stack-is-stack), hypothesis (3); sheaf input is etale-cohomology.tex, Tags 03O3 and 03O4; scheme-representable input from algebraic.tex, Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic)

proof.text: Let $(T_i\to T)$ be an etale covering and let $a_i:x|_{T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}x'|_{T_i}$ agree on overlaps. The isomorphism-sheaf condition for the assumed stack $\mathcal G$, as defined in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], glues the $q(a_i)$ uniquely to $b:q(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}q(x')$. In $K_{q(x')}$ compare $(x,b)$ with $(x',\mathrm{id})$. Their classes agree on the cover because of the arrows $a_i$, hence agree over $T$ by the uniqueness in step 2, using [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. The equivalence with the discrete groupoid $h_{P_T}(T)$ sends these two pairs to the same section. Its full faithfulness lifts the identity of that section to an arrow between the pairs, hence to $a:x\to x'$ with $q(a)=b$. The faithfulness in step 1 gives $a|_{T_i}=a_i$. If two global arrows restrict to these $a_i$, their images in $\mathcal G$ equal $b$ by its isomorphism-sheaf condition, and faithfulness makes the arrows equal. This proves that isomorphisms in $\mathcal F$ form sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0CKJ (lemma-relative-sheaf-over-stack-is-stack), proof, Descent for morphisms; scheme-representable input from algebraic.tex, Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic)

proof.text: Now let $x_i\in\mathcal F(T_i)$ and $\varphi_{ij}:x_j|_{T_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_i|_{T_{ij}}$, where $T_{ij}=T_i\times_TT_j$, be a descent datum, with $\varphi_{ij}\varphi_{jk}=\varphi_{ik}$ on triple overlaps. Applying $q$ gives such a datum in $\mathcal G$. By the assumed effective-object-descent condition of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], choose $y\in\mathcal G(T)$ and $\theta_i:q(x_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}y|_{T_i}$ with $\theta_i q(\varphi_{ij})=\theta_j$ on $T_{ij}$. Hence $\varphi_{ij}$ is an arrow in $K_y$ from $(x_j,\theta_j)$ to $(x_i,\theta_i)$ on that overlap. The classes of $(x_i,\theta_i)$ are consequently a matching family in the presheaf of step 2.

source.place: Tag 0CKJ (lemma-relative-sheaf-over-stack-is-stack), proof, Descent of objects, formation of the relative matching family; scheme-representable input from algebraic.tex, Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic)

proof.text: By existence of gluing from [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] as used in step 2, this matching family gives a section $s:T\to P_T$. Essential surjectivity of the assumed equivalence $K_y(T)\simeq h_{P_T}(T)$ provides a pair $(x,\theta)$ whose class corresponds to $s$. Over each $T_i$ its class equals that of $(x_i,\theta_i)$, so choose an arrow $\alpha_i:x|_{T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_i$ with $\theta_i q(\alpha_i)=\theta|_{T_i}$. On overlaps, $\theta_i q(\varphi_{ij}\alpha_j)=\theta_j q(\alpha_j)=\theta=\theta_i q(\alpha_i)$; cancelling $\theta_i$ and using faithfulness from step 1 yields $\varphi_{ij}\alpha_j=\alpha_i$. Thus the chosen local isomorphisms identify the original datum with pullback of $x$. Together with step 3 this is precisely the stack condition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].
